name: Burlington
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Burlington, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Burlington, MA: the Town Common tree lighting with fireworks and Santa, the 3rd Ave Holiday Stroll and a Polar Express PJ party.
lede: Burlington lights its town tree on the Town Common with fireworks and Santa, then fills Third Avenue with sleigh rides and free Santa photos.
celebrates: Burlington Parks and Recreation runs the town's Holiday Tree Lighting on the Town Common, an evening of live entertainment, fireworks and a visit from Santa that the department has held for more than fifty years. The 3rd Ave district hosts a Holiday Stroll with free Santa photos, sleigh rides, music and hot cocoa. Kings Dining and Entertainment on Second Avenue adds family holiday events, and the Burlington Mall runs a Santa Photo Experience. Parks and Recreation also offers holiday trips and craft workshops for older kids at the Rec Center.
lastyear: In 2025 Burlington planned its 52nd Annual Holiday Tree Lighting for Tuesday, December 2, at 5:30 pm on the Town Common, with live entertainment, fireworks and Santa. Snow pushed it back, and the town moved the lighting to Friday, December 5. The Burlington Mall's Santa Photo Experience ran from November 7 through December 24, and a local realty group held its 4th annual holiday home tour while collecting toys for Burlington WeeCare.
facts: The tree lighting on the Town Common reaches its 53rd year in 2026, so Burlington has been lighting a town tree there since the 1970s. The town plans a weather date each year, and 2025 showed why when snow moved the ceremony from Tuesday to Friday. Fireworks are part of the evening, which is not common for a December tree lighting. Local businesses sponsor the night each year.
trains: Burlington has no Commuter Rail station of its own. The closest stop is Anderson/Woburn station on the MBTA Lowell Line at 100 Atlantic Avenue in Woburn, a short drive east, with trains to North Station in Boston and north to Lowell. Kings in Burlington screens The Polar Express for families in pajamas. For a real holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a train through the Christmas lights, and Lowell has a streetcar museum.

faq: When is the Burlington tree lighting?

Burlington Parks and Recreation holds the Holiday Tree Lighting on the Town Common in early December, usually on a weeknight at 5:30 pm. The town sets a weather date, which it used in 2025 when snow moved the ceremony to a Friday. Check this page for the current year's date.
Is the Burlington tree lighting free?

Yes. The Holiday Tree Lighting on the Town Common is a free community event with live entertainment, fireworks and a visit from Santa. Local businesses sponsor it, so families do not need tickets. Burlington Parks and Recreation runs the evening and answers questions at 781-270-1695, including updates if snow moves the date.
Where can kids see Santa in Burlington?

Santa comes to the tree lighting on the Town Common, and the Holiday Stroll at 3rd Ave offers free printed photos with Santa and Mrs. Claus. The Burlington Mall also runs a Santa Photo Experience from early November through Christmas Eve.
Is there a train station in Burlington, MA?

No. The nearest MBTA Commuter Rail stop is Anderson/Woburn station on the Lowell Line at 100 Atlantic Avenue in Woburn. From there trains run to North Station in Boston and north to Lowell, so it is a short drive from Burlington.
